x: South London had five of the first six in the 3,000 metres event, but with only two to score Davies (8:54.4) and Black (9:11.6) were able to total 10 pts against the 15 of SLH, and thus kept our noses well to the front.
Kerr, Newell, Davies, Walker, Black, Dabbs, Linstead, Maclean. How's that for a line up to set a new 3 mile record?
Sandwiched between Black and Forey the four runners on "trial" were Davies, Dabbs, Thresher, and Miller. The two Johns won the day, but there was little else of interest to Belgrave.
Injuries to Kerr, Dabbs and Davies and the absence of our usual spear-head,Pat Newell, did not augur well for our chances before we had even left London.

Yet during our recent lean years, the name of Pat Newell has figured consistently and he has, along with other stalwarts like Walker, Linstead, Dabbs, Davies and Maclean, Helped keep the Belgrave flag flying, albeit a little limply.
(Davies) were now 11 seconds closer but Pompey (Gough) had gone back to 9th. STAGE 4: Chris Steer (16:04 - 2nd fastest)
Our scoring trio of Mann, O'Connor and Piotrowski only managed to pull back Davies, Franklin and Whitley of Thames Valley over the last two miles of the race.

The first of the short stages saw John setting off with Davies (TVH) haring after him. The "Valley" man swept past and went on to clock the fastest short stage time of the day but John was not put off in the slightest and brought us to the next take-over 23 seconds ahead of Hillingdon, now 3rd, and…
What a fine season JOHN BICOURT has been having. Now established as an international choice, John has only had Hollings and Davies to contend with amongst U.K.
At Johannesburg (6,500ft) he clocked 9:09.4 behind Bonzet (S.A) 8:56.8 and Davies (TVH/GB) 9:04.8, and at Pretoria (4,000ft) these three repeated their placings with 8:56.0, 8:57.6, 9:01.8.
Of course anything could happen and with rivals of the calibre of Davies, Staynings and Coates he will have to be in top form to make the team but he has plenty of determination.

Behind Ernie were top rated British sprinters Green, Hoyte and Roberts plus Davies of Jamaica. These performances added to Carl Lawton's fourth place in the 10km walk back in March give Belgrave a highly creditable 2nd and four 4ths for 1977.

You’ve gotta be winning the big ones to qualify as great in my book, and despite Moorcroft’s stunning times, he has recently penned an article about one of the big regrets of his career: that he never tasted victory in the National 12-stage. Have we poached Chris Davies, then?
